tts.stopConfirmTitle: What should happen to the server?
tts.stopConfirmBody: The Fish Speech server is running and holds roughly 17 GB of graphics memory. Stopping frees it; any playback in progress ends at once. Restarting stops it as well and brings it straight back up — the way to go when it is running but no longer answering properly. Either way the next sentence takes up to two minutes, because the model has to load again. Sentences already spoken stay in the cache and can still be played without a server.
tts.stopConfirmBodyStarting: The server is starting up and taking more graphics memory as it goes — up to roughly 17 GB. Stopping now ends the startup at once and frees everything it has taken. All you lose is the loading time spent so far; a later start begins again from scratch.

settings.fishOptionalDescription: Fish Speech is an additional GPU speech output with voice cloning. It is not required: Piper reads aloud without it. To set it up, enter the installation folder. Missing: {{missing}}

settings.seedDescription: Fixed seed keeps the same voice between requests.
settings.idleMinutesDescription: 0 means the server is never stopped automatically.
settings.maxCharsDescription: Longer texts are truncated to protect against accidental huge clipboards.
settings.compileDescription: Synthesis ALWAYS runs on the GPU — this switch only toggles the compile acceleration (~9× faster, RTF ~0.65 instead of ~6) at the cost of ~60 s longer server startup. Takes effect on the next server start; there is no CPU mode.
settings.volumeDescription: Playback volume for speech output, independent of feedback sounds.
settings.normalizeDescription: Levels every voice to the same loudness (-20 LUFS) — when recording or importing a reference and during playback. Without it, one speaker in a dialogue is too quiet and the next too loud.
settings.prewarmDescription: Brings the Fish Speech server up as soon as the app opens. It does not shorten the minute or so of loading — it runs while you are pasting a text or picking a voice anyway. Off by default, because the server takes roughly 17 GB of graphics memory while it does.
settings.enhanceDescription: Removes rumble and mains hum, lowers the noise in speaking pauses and evens out loud and quiet passages. Applies in three places: when recording or importing a voice, during playback, and when saving to a file. It matters most at recording time — Fish Speech models the voice from that take, including whatever is audible behind it.
settings.enhanceStrengthDescription: Gentle only cleans up and leaves the voice alone. Strong is for audibly noisy recordings and may colour the voice slightly.
settings.speedDescription: 0.5×–2×. Resampling slightly changes the pitch as well.
settings.exportFormatDescription: Format for saved audio files (voice changer, summaries). The server encodes directly.
settings.exportBitrateDescription: Sound quality and file size of the MP3 export. 192 kbps is plenty for speech; higher settings only pay off for music.
settings.contextMenuDescription: Adds "Read with Local Voice AI" to the right-click menu of TXT/MD/PDF/DOCX files. Note: Windows offers no system-wide menu for selected text — use the clipboard hotkey for that.
settings.autoTranscribeDescription: When you record or pick a reference, the app produces the transcript itself and fills it in; it stays editable. Switched off, the field stays empty and the text has to be typed — without a matching text Fish Speech learns the voice from the wrong words.
settings.engineDescription: Fish Speech sounds more natural and uses the graphics card. Piper runs on the CPU, starts instantly and needs no server — at the cost of a plainer voice.
settings.piperVoiceDescription: Which of the downloaded Piper voices reads aloud.

meetings.echoCancellationDescription: Removes the other party, which comes back from your speakers into the microphone, from your track so it does not appear twice as “Me” in the transcript. meetings.detectDescription: Notices when a program uses the microphone (Teams, Zoom, Webex, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, Skype, Signal or a browser) and shows a hint. Only Windows' usage log is read, never the microphone itself. It only ever shows a hint and never starts recording on its own.

meetings.diarizationDescription: After stopping, on import and on re-transcription, a local model detects who speaks when and labels the transcript with numbered speakers ("Gegenseite 1", "Person 2", ...). You can name the speakers in the transcript. Nothing that recognises a voice is stored. Takes effect from the next run.
meetings.selfNameDescription: Your own name in the transcript: your microphone ("Me") and, if the microphone is split into several people, the speaker with the largest share always carry this name, even if nobody addresses you. In People you are marked as "me". Leave empty to keep "Me".

A freshly opened microphone delivers no audio for 0.2 to 0.6 seconds, so the first words were lost; with the stream open every following dictation starts instantly. May degrade Bluetooth audio quality while active.

language.description: Language for meeting transcription — independent of the dictation setting. “Detect automatically” determines the language per recording from an audio sample and picks the suitable model; a fixed language wins over any detection. Transcription never translates: translations are created as their own version.

model.title: Transcription model
model.likeDictation: Automatic (Parakeet V3 GGUF, otherwise same as dictation)
model.description: Dedicated model for meetings and imports. Streaming models are tuned for live dictation — meetings transcribe in batches and profit from batch models like Parakeet V3. Automatic: Parakeet V3 GGUF Q8 (more accurate than the ONNX build) once downloaded under Models; otherwise the dictation model.
model.finalDescription: After stopping, a more accurate model rewrites the whole transcript; AI notes are created only afterwards. Automatic: with a graphics card Whisper Large v3 (otherwise Qwen3-ASR 1.7B), without one the live transcript stays. A model picked explicitly also runs without a graphics card; an hour of meeting then takes about a quarter of an hour.
model.parallelDescription: How many files are transcribed at the same time. More than one only while memory (and graphics memory) suffice for each additional one – each loads the model again. Otherwise the next file waits (“waiting for memory”). A running recording always takes priority: the queue pauses then.
